_doc: Fixtures for .harmony/probe-crossfade.sh (s-rta-0926 xfade lane). @MEDIA@ is replaced at run time with the checkout's media/ dir. 'crossfade' cases: one layer, column 0 = OUT clip, column 1 = IN clip, Dissolve over transitionSpeed seconds; the probe renders IN-only and OUT-only references first, then triggers OUT -> IN and asserts every mid frame lies strictly between them. 'still' cases: single-state renders of the other sites in the same bug class (a texture held while a later pass writes the same FBO).

a_both_effected.why: THE BUG: incoming clip fx land in effectTex_A_, the outgoing clip's fx chain (run inside applyTransition) overwrote effectTex_A_, dissolve sampled the outgoing clip on both inputs

b_only_incoming_effected.why: control: outgoing chain is empty, so nothing writes the scratch pair after the incoming fx

c_only_outgoing_effected.why: control: incoming texture is the image itself, never a scratch texture

e_two_effects_each.why: class: the outgoing chain's second pass needs a scratch target that is neither its own input nor the held incoming result (the third pool slot)

f_same_source_type.why: class: both clips are the same procedural source type, which shares ONE output FBO; rendering the outgoing clip overwrote the incoming clip's texture

g_drywet_second_effect.why: class: dry/wet blend of a NON-first effect drew into the texture it sampled as u_original. Asserted as MIX == (1-w)*DRY + w*WET, all three rendered live

h_transparent_layer_transform.why: class: a Transparent layer with a layer transform keyed scratchTex_ (the transform's output) into scratchFBO_. Asserted equal (RGB) to the same layer as Opaque, whose path never keys

i_layer_router_self.why: class: a Layer Router clip routed to its own layer handed saveLayerOutput its own output texture as the source (draw into the texture being sampled). Expected: the layer holds its previous output (the image)

j_temporal_clip_vs_layer_chain.why: class: a layer's clip chain and layer chain shared ONE temporal buffer (u_prev_frame, keyed by layer id), so each chain's previous frame was the other chain's output. Clip [Freeze 0.5] + layer [Invert 1.0, Freeze 0.5] must settle on the inverted image, same as layer [Invert 1.0] alone (both Freezes converge on their own input)
